s6616: The driver should be aware that the road is most often icy:
s6614: On the central streets of built-up areas
s6617: According to subparagraph "d" of paragraph 10 of Article 25 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, when driving on a road the driver must take the following into account: on an icy stretch of road, the driver should avoid braking, changing speed and changing direction sharply as far as possible. The driver should also be aware that the road is most often icy on bridges, overpasses and flyovers.
s6621: When driving in rain or snow, the driver must bear in mind that:
s6618: The time and distance needed to brake the vehicle increase, and precipitation also reduces visibility
s6620: It is advisable to reduce the distance between their vehicle and the vehicle ahead
s6622: According to subparagraph "e" of paragraph 10 of Article 25 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, when driving on a road the driver must take the following into account: since the time and distance needed to brake the vehicle increase when driving in rain or snow, and precipitation also reduces visibility, the driver must reduce speed and increase the distance between their vehicle and the vehicle ahead.
s6625: When there are puddles on the road, the driver must bear in mind that:
s6623: Steering and braking the vehicle become more difficult, and there is a high risk of the vehicle skidding
s6624: It is advisable to speed up when driving through a puddle
s6626: According to subparagraph "i" of paragraph 10 of Article 25 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, when driving on a road the driver must take the following into account: when there are puddles on the road, the driver must bear in mind that steering and braking the vehicle become more difficult, and there is also a high risk of the vehicle skidding (especially with worn tyres or at high speed).
s6630: Driving a vehicle at high speed for a long time causes:
s6627: A drop in the driver's concentration and in their sense of high speed
s6628: Failure of the vehicle's braking system
s6629: All of the effects listed in this question
s6631: According to subparagraph "m" of paragraph 10 of Article 25 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, when driving on a road the driver must take the following into account: driving at high speed for a long time reduces concentration and the sense of high speed.
s6634: Unless the traffic arrangements on the road provide otherwise, on a road with two or three carriageways the driver of a vehicle is prohibited from:
s6632: Moving onto the carriageway intended for traffic in the opposite direction
s6633: Changing lanes on the carriageway intended for traffic in their own direction
s6635: According to paragraph 6 of Article 31 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, unless the traffic arrangements on the road provide otherwise, on a road with two or three carriageways the driver of a vehicle is prohibited from moving onto the carriageway intended for traffic in the opposite direction.
s6638: Does the driver's emotional state affect road safety?
s6639: The driver's emotional state affects road safety.
s6643: How does fatigue affect a driver's attention and reactions on the road?
s6640: Attention drops and reaction time increases
s6641: Attention drops and reaction time decreases
s6642: Neither attention nor reaction time changes
s6644: Driver fatigue reduces attention and increases reaction time.
s6645: Which of the road sign combinations shown indicate the days of the week on which the sign applies?
s6649: At night and in conditions of insufficient visibility, we perceive the speed of an oncoming vehicle as:
s6647: The same as it really is
s6650: In daylight, the human eye judges the speed of an oncoming vehicle by comparing it with other reference points around it (road signs, markings, roadside greenery and so on), whereas at night and in conditions of insufficient visibility we can orient ourselves only by the light of the headlights, so we perceive the speed of an oncoming vehicle as lower than it really is.
s6651: As a vehicle's speed increases, the grip of the tyres on the road:
s6652: As a vehicle's speed increases, the grip of the tyres on the road decreases.
s6655: When overtaking by moving into the lane for oncoming traffic, one of the main causes of accidents is that the driver judges the speed of the oncoming vehicle as:
s6656: When overtaking by moving into the lane for oncoming traffic, one of the main causes of accidents is that the driver judges the speed of the oncoming vehicle as lower than it really is.
s6660: When driving at high speed on a straight road for a long time, the driver perceives the vehicle's speed as:
s6659: The same as it really is
s6661: When driving at high speed on a straight road for a long time, the driver perceives the vehicle's speed as lower than it really is.
s6665: How does the driver's field of vision change as the vehicle's speed increases?
s6664: The field of vision does not change
s6666: As the vehicle's speed increases, the driver's field of vision narrows.
s6667: When driving in fog, we perceive the distance to objects as:
s6668: When driving in fog, we perceive the distance to objects as greater than it really is.
s6672: In the territory of Georgia, the driver must carry a duly certified translation of the vehicle registration document and the driving licence if the information in them:
s6669: Is not written in Georgian or Latin letters
s6670: Is not written in Latin letters, but is written in Georgian letters
s6671: Is not written in Georgian letters, but is written in Latin letters
s6673: According to subparagraphs "a" and "b" of paragraph 17 of Article 21 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, the driver of a vehicle of a category or subcategory defined by Article 54 of this Law must carry the following and, at the request of an authorised person of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Georgia, must stop the vehicle and present them to that person: a) a document, valid in the territory of Georgia, confirming the right to drive a vehicle of the category or subcategory they are driving, as well as the document confirming the registration of that vehicle (unless the legislation of Georgia provides otherwise); b) a duly certified translation of the document(s) referred to in subparagraph "a" of this paragraph, if the information in that document/those documents is not written in Georgian or Latin letters.
s6674: When the owner is not present and the driver crosses the state border in the owner's vehicle, or enters a part of the country where Georgia's jurisdiction does not apply, must the driver carry a document confirming their authority to possess, use or dispose of that vehicle?
s6675: According to subparagraph "c" of paragraph 17 of Article 21 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, the driver of a vehicle of a category or subcategory defined by Article 54 of this Law must carry, and, at the request of an authorised person of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Georgia, must stop the vehicle and present to that person, a document confirming their authority to possess, dispose of or use that vehicle when, in the owner's absence, they cross the state border in the owner's vehicle or enter a part of the country where Georgia's jurisdiction does not apply.
s6679: When tram tracks run along the middle of the carriageway of a two-way road, level with it, what is considered to separate the two directions of traffic?
s6676: The imaginary centre line between the tram tracks for opposite directions
s6677: The right-hand track of the trams travelling in the same direction
s6678: The left-hand track of the trams travelling in the opposite direction
s6680: According to paragraph 3 of Article 31 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, on a two-way road where tram tracks run along the middle of the carriageway, level with it, the imaginary centre line between the tram tracks for opposite directions is considered to separate the two directions of traffic.
s6682: How many carriageways does this road have?
s6683: According to paragraph 15 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, the carriageway of a road (carriageway) is the element of a road intended for trackless vehicles (other than the sidewalk, the shoulder, the cycle path and the footpath). According to paragraph 12 of the same Article, a road is the entire surface of a road or street open to traffic. A road may have a single carriageway, or several carriageways clearly separated by a dividing strip or located at different levels. The term may include tram tracks, sidewalks, shoulders, dividing strips and cycle paths.
s6687: Of the places listed below, where does the law allow a driver to use whichever lane is most convenient for them?
s6684: In a built-up area, on a road that has at least two lanes for traffic in the same direction, marked with longitudinal markings
s6685: Both outside and inside built-up areas, on any section of the carriageway where driving faster than 80 km/h is permitted
s6686: On any road in a built-up area, if the driver is driving a slow-moving vehicle
s6688: According to paragraph 13 of Article 34 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, subject to the requirements of Article 31 of this Law (except paragraph 5), in a built-up area, on a road that has at least two lanes for traffic in the same direction, marked with longitudinal markings, the driver may use whichever lane is most convenient for them (except in cases provided for by this Law). They may move into another lane only in accordance with the rules for turning right or left, overtaking, stopping or parking.
s6693: In which of the following cases is the driver of a motor vehicle not required to wear a seat belt while driving on the road?
s6689: If the motor vehicle was not designed with seat belts
s6690: If the driver is a person with disabilities
s6691: If the driver is driving an emergency service vehicle
s6692: If the driver is driving in a built-up area
s6697: In which of the following cases is a vehicle in the territory of a state considered to be in "international traffic"?
s6694: Only if it is not registered in that state
s6695: Only if it has been brought into the country temporarily, for no longer than the period set by that state's legislation
s6696: Only if it belongs to a natural or legal person whose normal place of residence is outside that state
s6698: According to paragraph 66 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, international traffic: a vehicle in the territory of a state is considered to be in international traffic if it: a) belongs to a natural or legal person whose normal place of residence is outside that state; b) is not registered in that state; c) has been brought into that state temporarily, for no longer than the period set by its legislation. Note: a vehicle combination is considered to be in international traffic if at least one vehicle in it meets the requirements set out in this paragraph.
s6700: On all roads in Georgia, traffic must drive:
s6699: On both the left-hand and the right-hand side
s6701: According to paragraph 1 of Article 31 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, on all roads in Georgia traffic is set to drive on the right.
s6705: On a two-way road with a dividing strip, the side for traffic in the opposite direction is:
s6702: The carriageway to the left of the dividing strip
s6703: The carriageway to the right of the dividing strip
s6704: None of those listed in this question
s6706: According to paragraph 3 of Article 31 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, on a two-way road with a dividing strip, the side for traffic in the opposite direction is the carriageway to the left of the dividing strip.
s6709: Without a special reason, may a driver hinder other vehicles by driving excessively slowly?
s6707: Yes, if they are driving in the far right lane
s6708: Yes, because the traffic rules only prohibit exceeding the maximum permitted speed
s6710: According to paragraph 3 of Article 33 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a driver must not, without a special reason, hinder other vehicles by driving excessively slowly.
s6713: If the requirements of a temporary road sign mounted on a vehicle of an organisation carrying out roadworks contradict the requirements of a permanently installed road sign on the same section of road, the driver must follow:
s6711: The requirements of the temporary road sign mounted on the roadworks organisation's vehicle
s6712: The requirements of the permanently installed road sign
s6718: The plate confirming that a car has passed its roadworthiness test is placed on the windscreen, in the:
s6719: According to paragraph 7 of Article 11 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, the plate confirming that a car has passed its roadworthiness test is placed on the car, in the bottom left corner of the windscreen.
s6723: A motorcycle, bus, car or truck may only be driven by a person:
s6720: Who meets all of the conditions listed in this question
s6721: Who has been granted the right to drive a vehicle of the relevant category and/or subcategory in the manner established by the legislation of Georgia, and whose right has not been suspended or terminated
s6722: Whose state of health meets the health requirements for driving vehicles set by the legislation of Georgia
s6724: According to paragraph 1 of Article 54 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, only a person who meets the following conditions has the right to drive a vehicle of a category and/or subcategory defined by this Article: a) their state of health meets the health requirements for driving vehicles set by the legislation of Georgia; b) they have been granted the right to drive a vehicle of the relevant category and/or subcategory in the manner established by the legislation of Georgia, and this right has not been suspended, revoked or terminated (cancelled).
s6725: A person with the right to drive category "B" vehicles may also drive vehicles of which subcategory?
s6729: Handing over a motor vehicle for another person to drive is prohibited:
s6726: In any of the cases listed in this question
s6727: Only if the person does not have the right to drive a vehicle of the relevant category or subcategory, or this right has been suspended, revoked or terminated (cancelled) in the manner established by the legislation of Georgia
s6728: Only if the person is under the influence of alcohol, drugs or psychotropic substances
s6730: According to paragraphs 4 and 5 of Article 20 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic: 4. It is prohibited to hand over a vehicle to be driven by a person who is under the influence of alcohol, drugs or psychotropic substances. 5. It is prohibited to hand over a vehicle to be driven by a person who does not have the right to drive a vehicle of the relevant category or subcategory, or whose right has been suspended, revoked or terminated (cancelled) in the manner established by the legislation of Georgia.
s6731: Is a driver whose state of health does not meet the health requirements for driving vehicles prohibited from driving a vehicle?
s6732: According to paragraph 2 of Article 21 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a driver whose state of health does not meet the health requirements for driving vehicles is prohibited from driving a vehicle.
s6736: Under the requirements of the European Agreement concerning the Work of Crews of Vehicles engaged in International Road Transport (AETR), a driver in international traffic must ensure:
s6733: Both that they drive with a properly working tachograph and that they observe the rules on working and rest periods
s6734: Only that they observe the rules on working and rest periods
s6735: Only that they drive with a properly working tachograph
s6737: According to paragraph 19 of Article 21 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a driver in international traffic must ensure, in accordance with the requirements of the European Agreement concerning the Work of Crews of Vehicles engaged in International Road Transport (AETR), that they drive with a properly working recording device (tachograph), and that they observe the rules on working and rest periods.
s6739: May a pedestrian walk on the carriageway if there is no footpath, sidewalk or roadside, or if it is impossible to use them?
s6738: Yes, and when walking on the carriageway they must keep as close as possible to its edge
s6740: According to paragraph 4 of Article 24 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, if there is no footpath, sidewalk or roadside, or if it is impossible to use them, a pedestrian may walk on the carriageway. If there is a cycle path and the traffic density allows it, pedestrians may walk on it, but they must not hinder the movement of bicycles and mopeds. According to paragraph 6 of the same Article, in the cases provided for in paragraphs 2, 4 and 5 of this Article, a pedestrian walking on the carriageway must keep as close as possible to the edge of the carriageway.
s6744: A "bus" is a motor vehicle designed:
s6741: To carry passengers, with more than 8 seats
s6742: To carry passengers, with no more than 8 seats, not counting the driver's seat
s6743: To carry goods, with a maximum permitted mass of more than 12 000 kg
s6745: According to paragraph 1 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a bus is a motor vehicle designed to carry passengers, with more than 8 seats, not counting the driver's seat.
s6746: A combination of a truck and a trailer (trailers) with a maximum permitted mass of more than 750 kg
s6747: A combination of a bus and a trailer (trailers) with a maximum permitted mass of more than 1200 kg
s6748: A combination of a car and a trailer (trailers) with a maximum permitted mass of more than 750 kg
s6750: According to paragraph 3 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a road train is a combination of a truck and a trailer/trailers with a maximum permitted mass of more than 750 kg.
s6751: A specialised motor vehicle designed to carry cars and light wheeled tractors
s6752: A truck used to carry dangerous goods
s6753: Any motor vehicle with a maximum permitted mass of more than 12 000 kg that is designed to be operated with a trailer
s6755: According to paragraph 4 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a car transporter is a specialised motor vehicle designed to carry cars and light wheeled tractors.
s6756: A trailer designed to be coupled to a motor vehicle in such a way that part of it rests on the vehicle, and a significant part of the mass of the semi-trailer and its load is carried by the vehicle
s6757: A two-axle trailer designed to be towed by any motor vehicle with a rigid coupling
s6759: According to paragraph 51 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a "semi-trailer" is a trailer designed to be coupled to a motor vehicle in such a way that part of it rests on the vehicle, and a significant part of the mass of the semi-trailer and its load is carried by the vehicle.
s6760: A motor vehicle designed to carry goods, with a maximum permitted mass of more than 3 500 kg
s6761: Any motor vehicle designed to carry goods
s6762: Any motor vehicle designed to carry goods, with a gross mass of no more than 3 500 kg
s6764: According to paragraph 71 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a "truck" is a motor vehicle designed to carry goods, with a maximum permitted mass of more than 3 500 kg.
s6765: The part of the vehicle's actual mass that presses on an axle and so creates a load on the road
s6766: The maximum mass on each axle set by the manufacturer, the sum of which determines the limit of the vehicle's gross mass
s6768: According to paragraph 88 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, "axle load" is the part of the vehicle's actual mass that presses on an axle and so creates a load on the road. When determining the load on each drive or non-drive axle, structurally separate axles located in one line across the vehicle are treated as a single axle.
s6772: When determining the load on each drive or non-drive axle, structurally separate axles located in one line across the vehicle are treated as:
s6771: A single axle in the case of a non-drive axle, and independent axles in the case of a drive axle
s6773: According to paragraph 88 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, axle load is the part of the vehicle's actual mass that presses on an axle and so creates a load on the road. When determining the load on each drive or non-drive axle, structurally separate axles located in one line across the vehicle are treated as a single axle.
s6776: Is it permitted to carry so many passengers, or to carry them in such a way, that this hinders driving or restricts the driver's field of view?
s6774: Yes, but only with the driver's consent
s6775: Yes, but only outside built-up areas, on a secondary road, provided the vehicle's speed does not exceed 40 km/h
s6777: According to paragraph 1 of Article 46 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, it is prohibited to carry so many passengers, or to carry them in such a way, that this hinders driving the vehicle or restricts the driver's field of view.
s6782: Any load on a vehicle must be placed and, where necessary, secured so that during transport:
s6778: All of the conditions listed in this question are met
s6779: Only that visibility and the field of view are not restricted, the stability of the vehicle is not affected and it is not made harder to drive
s6780: Only that it does not cover the lights, brake lights, direction indicators, reflectors, registration number or distinguishing sign of the state of registration, or the hand signals provided for by this Law
s6781: Only that it does not endanger other road users, does not damage state, public or private property, and does not drag along or fall onto the road
s6783: According to subparagraphs "a", "b" and "c" of paragraph 11 of Article 47 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, any load on a vehicle must be placed and, where necessary, secured so that during transport: a) it does not endanger other road users, does not damage state, public or private property, and does not drag along or fall onto the road; b) it does not restrict visibility or the field of view, does not affect the stability of the vehicle and does not make it harder to drive; c) it does not cover the vehicle's lights, brake lights, direction indicators, reflectors, registration number or distinguishing sign of the state of registration, or the hand signals provided for by this Law.
s6788: When placing and/or securing a load to be carried on a vehicle, which of the following requirements is not mandatory?
s6784: All of the requirements listed in this question are mandatory
s6785: Visibility and the field of view must not be restricted, the stability of the vehicle must not be affected, and it must not be made harder to drive
s6786: The lights, brake lights, direction indicators, reflectors, registration number and distinguishing sign of the state of registration, as well as hand signals, must not be covered
s6787: Other road users must not be endangered, state, public or private property must not be damaged, and the load must not drag along or fall onto the road
s6789: According to subparagraphs "a", "b" and "c" of paragraph 11 of Article 47 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, any load on a vehicle must be placed and, where necessary, secured so that during transport: a) it does not endanger other road users, does not damage state, public or private property, and does not drag along or fall onto the road; b) it does not restrict visibility or the field of view, does not affect the stability of the vehicle and does not make it harder to drive; c) it does not cover the vehicle's lights, brake lights, direction indicators, reflectors, registration number or distinguishing sign of the state of registration, or the hand signals provided for by this Law.
s6793: When driving round a bend, in which case is a car most resistant to overturning?
s6791: With a load, but without passengers
s6792: With passengers, but without a load
s6796: On a two-way road without a dividing strip, a group of children must walk:
s6794: On the shoulder, walking against the direction of traffic
s6795: On the shoulder, walking in the direction of traffic
s6797: According to paragraph 5 of Article 26 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, on a two-way road without a dividing strip, a group of children must walk on the shoulder against the direction of traffic.
s6798: Which of these road signs shows that traffic may only go straight ahead?
s6799: Which of these road signs permits traffic to go only to the right?
s6800: The direction for going around a dividing strip, traffic island or any other obstacle on the right only
s6801: Entry onto a one-way road or carriageway
s6803: According to subparagraph "c" of the Note to paragraphs 4.1.1–4.1.6 of Chapter 4 (Mandatory signs) of Annex 1 to the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, signs 4.1.1–4.1.6 do not apply to route vehicles.
s6804: Which of these road signs shows the direction for going around a dividing strip, traffic island or any other obstacle on the left only?
s6805: Which of these road signs shows that traffic may go right or left?
s6806: According to paragraph 4.1.6 of Chapter 4 (Mandatory signs) of Annex 1 to the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic and subparagraph "a" of the Note to that paragraph, road sign 4.1.6 "Turn right or left only" permits traffic only in the directions shown by the arrows.
s6807: Which of these road signs marks a path for pedestrians that is separate from the road?
s6808: According to paragraph 4.5 of Chapter 4 (Mandatory signs) of Annex 1 to the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, road sign 4.5 "Footpath" marks a path for pedestrians that is separate from the road. Sign 4.5 is placed as the main sign at the start of the footpath, and is repeated after every place where the footpath crosses a road.
s6809: Which of these road signs shows the direction in which vehicles carrying dangerous goods are permitted to travel?
s6810: According to paragraphs 4.9.1–4.9.3 of Chapter 4 (Mandatory signs) of Annex 1 to the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, road signs 4.9.1–4.9.3 "Direction of travel for vehicles carrying dangerous goods" show the permitted direction of travel for vehicles carrying dangerous goods which, under the legislation of Georgia, must display the "Dangerous goods" identification sign: 4.9.1 – straight ahead, 4.9.2 – right, 4.9.3 – left.
s6811: May the truck driver continue in the direction of the arrow?
s6812: According to paragraph 4.1.2 of Chapter 4 (Mandatory signs) of Annex 1 to the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic and subparagraph "a" of the Note to that paragraph, road sign 4.1.2 "Turn right only" permits traffic only in the directions shown by the arrows. According to paragraphs 8.4.1–8.4.8 of Chapter 8 (Additional information signs) of the same Annex, plates 8.4.1–8.4.8 "Type of vehicle" show the type of vehicle to which the sign applies, and according to subparagraph "a" of the Note to that Chapter, plate 8.4.1 makes the sign apply to trucks (with or without a trailer) with a maximum permitted mass of more than 3.5 t.
